title: Retire legacy batch-embed transport (batch-embed-mk1) and provide client adapter playbook
creator: Olivia Park
description: This ticket defines the product requirements and acceptance criteria for retiring the legacy batch-embed transport (internal name: batch-embed-mk1) and the embedded model alias embed-old-1. It provides a prescriptive adapter playbook for client SDKs, CLI, and common partner integrations to migrate to the unified embeddings endpoint (embeddings.v2) and the newer model aliases. The goal is to minimize customer disruption and provide clear telemetry gates and rollback plans.
background: batch-embed-mk1 was implemented in 2022 to support high-throughput batch uploads with a custom transport and response streaming format. Since then the platform standardized on embeddings.v2 which supports bulk uploads with improved backpressure, consistent trace IDs, and structured error responses. Maintaining two transports increases operational burden, leads to inconsistent telemetry, and prevents unified rate-limiting and cost accounting.
goals: Announce and execute a phased retirement of batch-embed-mk1 and embed-old-1 alias with minimal customer API breakages
Provide SDK adapter changes and example migration snippets in JS/Python/Go
Ensure telemetry gates track migration progress and catch quality regressions
Offer runtime fallbacks and partner support windows for enterprise customers
out_of_scope: Changing embeddings model quality or retraining models
Major surface changes to embeddings.v2 schema (only compatibility shims allowed)
On-prem/private deployment packaging for customers on custom runtimes (handled as separate initiative)
timeline_milestones: 2026-03-10: Internal PRD approved and engineering kickoff
2026-03-24: SDK adapter PRs (JS/Python/Go) opened with docs draft
2026-04-07: Canary traffic for embeddings.v2 enabled for 20% of inbound batch requests
2026-04-21: Public deprecation announcement and migration guide published
2026-05-05: Start enforcement of deprecation warnings (3xx/429 guidance) in logs and telemetry
2026-05-15: batch-embed-mk1 write path disabled for new requests; read-only grace window begins
2026-06-15: Complete shutdown of batch-embed-mk1; final audit and billing reconciliation
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal): Engineering integration tests and interop with batching gateway
Phase 1 (Canary): Route 20% of batch requests to embeddings.v2 with transparent proxy and compare outputs
Phase 2 (Early Access): Opt-in customers invited to migrate with dedicated success engineering support
Phase 3 (Public): Deprecation notice published, automated client adapters available in official SDKs
Phase 4 (Enforcement): Stop accepting new write requests to batch-embed-mk1; continued read-only grace
Phase 5 (Shutdown): Full shutdown and removal from model catalog and docs
migration_steps_for_clients: Identify integrations calling batch-embed-mk1 or using alias embed-old-1
Update request envelope to match embeddings.v2 bulk format (see examples in SDKs)
Switch model alias from embed-old-1 to embed-unified-v2 or embed-recommended alias
Validate outputs end-to-end with canary traffic; compare vector lengths, normalization, and downstream scoring
Update retry/backoff to use standard embeddings rate limits and handle structured 429/5xx responses
Remove custom transport parsing logic and use SDK adapter methods for streaming/async uploads
sdk_changes: JS SDK: add embeddings.bulkFromFile() adapter that converts legacy payloads and warns at runtime
Python SDK: add EmbeddingsAdapter class with migrate_batch_legacy() helper and CLI migration flag
Go SDK: provide batchshim package that preserves legacy semantics while calling embeddings.v2
Doc PRs with code examples, unit tests, and migration checklist for each SDK
backend_changes: Gateway: implement transparent proxy that mirrors batch-embed-mk1 writes to embeddings.v2 for canary
Rate limiting: ensure unified rate bucket for embeddings.v2 covers migrated traffic
Billing: tag migrated requests for accurate cost attribution during grace period
telemetry_and_gates: Migration coverage: percent of legacy requests successfully routed to embeddings.v2 (target >= 95% before enforcement)
Quality regressions: downstream MRR/recall metric regressions tied to evaluation prompt sets (< 1% acceptable)
Error spike gate: if 5xx or 4xx increases > 2x baseline in canary, block rollout and roll back proxy
Adoption thresholds: require >= 70% of active customers with legacy calls to be notified and engaged before enforcement
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Vector format mismatch causes downstream model scoring issues. Mitigation: provide automated payload diff tool and test harness
Risk: Enterprise customers on Private deployments cannot upgrade. Mitigation: offer extended support and config toggle for longer grace
Risk: SDKs introduce regressions. Mitigation: coordinated release dates and cross-SDK regression test job in CI
Risk: Billing attribution errors. Mitigation: tag and reconcile billing daily during migration window
acceptance_criteria: Official SDKs publish adapter methods and migration examples with tests merged to main
Telemetry shows >=95% of legacy batch requests successfully mirrored and validated in embeddings.v2 during canary
No critical quality regression observed on evaluation prompt set (defined in PRD) after canary run
Customer communication artifacts (blog post, migration guide, support playbook) are published and reviewed by legal and support
Rollback plan and automated proxy disable are implemented and tested in staging
